paragraphs: Chapter 931
Episode 231. Determination (4)
The land where the Castle of the Holy King once stood was changing rapidly, crumbling like bones. A sharp, violet magic energy surged between the hideously gaping cracks.
There were hundreds of them. They moved like fingers, violently tearing the less cracked ground apart. The sound was chilling, akin to forcing disjointed bone joints together.
At a glance, the ground beneath looked like a spread of violet sea. It seemed like a sea of agony, capable of tearing at the mind of anyone who faced it, opening its maw wide.
‘Fanatics...!’
It was clear that the space where the eternal warehouse had been was already completely corroded by the magic. It meant that the chances of Lani's survival were extremely slim.
The holy kingdom was collapsing.
Over 70% of the territory was under indiscriminate attack, and the Castle of the Holy King had vanished without a trace.
Even if this war ends in victory for the Vamel Alliance, the damage is irreversible.

"Black Dragon Murakan, you really live up to your name, huh? I never thought you'd be able to block my authority to this extent. But still, the Castle of the Holy King is now dust, and although the body of the Earth Lord you dared imprison has awakened."
Now is not the time to grieve Lani's death.
Murakan's eyes were colder and harder than ever. There were still many people alive in the holy kingdom.
He had to protect even one more person. Murakan's duty remained the same. The sole reason he left his position and flew to the Castle of the Holy King was just that.
Talaris read Murakan's intent as he spread the curtain in the sky again. She took a deep breath and gently grasped her sword.
She decided not to use a technique that would burden her tired body. She also decided not to fend off such an enemy attack directly. Especially since Murakan like that said he would protect her.
Murakan did not even breathe towards Bideluche. He did not attack with Dark Arrival or Black Suppression either. He was solely focused on protecting his comrades and the people.
"Oh my, the atmosphere of the Archery Master has changed a bit? What, is it like a secret weapon?"
"If it's not a fight determined by the size of power or authority, but pure close combat. There is only one person in this world who can defeat me."
"What?"
"So you should have inflicted a fatal wound on me before Murakan came, Bideluche."
Whoosh, whooosh!
The violet beams flying towards Talaris were all blocked by the barrier of spiritual energy. Talaris began to rush without even paying attention to Bideluche's long-range containment.
"'What, Murakan can protect the Archer Lord to this extent?'
It was something completely unexpected for Videluche. He was sure that Murakan would only provide a certain level of protection at best.
During the time Talaris narrowed the gap by hundreds of steps, not a single one of Videluche's beams or energy attacks threatened Talaris.
Videluche is not a caster.
Therefore, to penetrate Murakan's spirit after he has made his resolve, he too had to risk something. With his arrogant attitude and gaze, he could never undermine Murakan's will.
Shiit-!

Before he knew it, Talaris, who had closed the gap completely, stabbed his sword into Videluche's chest. Videluche responded immediately by throwing his fist and exploding his magic in all directions.
He was trying to push Talaris back. However, Talaris did not even need to avoid the magic that exploded right in front of him. The spirit mingling with Talaris' shadow was protecting her.
"Hup!"
Videluche gasped for breath. He should have created a gap, but instead, Talaris was even closer, swinging her frost blade.
The frost blade held an unbelievably weak chill. It could not inflict any damage on its own, but the sword itself was what made Videluche feel cold.
'The Archer Lord's sword keeps penetrating deeper than I expect. I think I've dodged it, but it touches me, I'm sure I've blocked it, but it's just an illusion.'
It's incredibly sharp.
Videluche felt this way about Talaris' sword. Although the power contained in the sword was far from enough to tear his flesh, he couldn't simply engage in a fight by exposing his body.

Therefore, now it was Videluche who kept trying to create a gap. If he got close, he felt like he would be deeply cut, and the ranged attacks he fired from a distance were all blocked by Murakan, making the fight frustrating.
'But anyway, a tired body will collapse as time passes. Besides, Murakan also can't care about the Archer Lord forever.'
However, time was definitely on the side of the underworld.
Zito, who had just woken up, did not attack them yet because he was still forming his figure, but the moment it was completed, it was bound to tear Murakan's barrier into pieces.
'Besides, Phaelito will soon kill them and join us, so there's no need to worry about any tricky tactics.'
At most 5 minutes.
In Videluche's view, the time when Murakan and Talaris could gain some advantage was only about that long. Within that time, there was absolutely no chance that he would be fatally injured or killed.
"You have good intuition. I thought you were just an arrogant fool."
"Yeah, it's frustrating, isn't it? It seems like something could happen if I just fight against you, but I don't. By the way, your black dragon has an amazing patience."
Talaris looked around.
The energy of Zito, which was released at the site of Seongwangsung, was getting thicker. Purple ribbons were embedded in various parts of Murakan's wide spirit barrier."
Murakan didn't make a sound, but Videluche knew how excruciating the pain was.
"Enduring the pain of Lord Zito's true energy seeping into every part of your body. It seems like Lord Zito will enjoy this for quite some time."
Murakan didn't respond and continued to focus.
He could easily avoid Zito's energy if he wanted to. But if he didn't take it, the purple bands would go to the people he needed to protect.
Fighting to protect something from those who only sought to destroy, steal, and trample always ended up like this.
Unless he was overwhelmingly stronger than the enemy, he would constantly be pushed back.
Murakan's scales were shaking one by one and falling off. Each scale that fell was dyed purple and flowed into the origin of the band.
Zito's eye was stealing Murakan's power. If this continued, permanent damage would start in about ten minutes.
He wasn't scared of that.
Even if he lost his power like before, it was fine as long as he could recover gradually. After all, Jin is not so weak that he needs his protection anymore.
But what made Murakan uneasy now was the process of Zito's eye taking shape. Despite not knowing the exact power and abilities of Zito's eye, instinct was telling him it was definitely dangerous.
'There's only one chance. I have to fully release my spiritual energy and spread the dark dawn of Jin. Even if successful, it will take about five hundred years to recuperate.'
Murakan made up his mind.

Maybe it would take more than recuperation and he would have to fall into a long sleep like a thousand years ago. But that was better than losing everything Jin wanted to protect. That's what Murakan thought.
'Strawberry pie, it's hard to say goodbye...'
The moment Murakan thought that far,
Suddenly, the bands that had shot up to the sky were severed and fell. The sword that cut the bands was Sharl.
"I'm sorry for being late, Lord Murakan."

Luntia had just arrived in the Holy Kingdom, piercing through the magical energy of Phaelito. As soon as she entered the Holy Kingdom, she cut down the bands embedded around the spiritual energy barrier and dropped them.
Are you okay? What about the youngest?
Luntia didn't ask anything.
The fact that Jin and Murakan are separated, and the only reason why Murakan isn't shouting to save Jin first despite that, is for one reason only.
"It seems that the Lord has ordered us to guard the Holy Kingdom. I'll carry it out."
Luna's request of 'please take care of Jin' was not a priority over the absolute command of the Lord.
[I could have used the extra hands. Are you alone?]
"Yes, but many superhumans including the first generation plan to join as soon as the defense of the main base is complete. What I need to cut is that."
Luntia pointed her sword, Sharl, at the ground where Zito's energy was gushing out.
"Hey, buddy? Do you know what you're blabbering about cutting something, urgh!"
The cold sword just grazed Videluche's neck.
"You seem to have forgotten whom you're facing. Let me engrave it in your memory again, and it will be your last."
Luntia didn't even glance at Videluche and Tallaris.
Not because she was ignoring them, but because she trusted Tallaris. If it was this kind of close combat, there was no chance she would lose to Videluche.
Besides, she didn't have the luxury to keep an eye on them.
The moment she faced Zito's eye directly, Luntia also started to experience the same pain as Murakan.
[I will focus on Bigungju for a moment while taking care of my body, don’t push yourself too much.]
"I understand, Lord Murakan."
"Did you say you felt stronger for the first time in a while earlier?"
Phaelito approached the fallen Jin and spoke.
Jin hurriedly got up, but Phaelito had no intention of killing him immediately. He had several opportunities to finish Jin and Dante, but Phaelito kept them alive to create a more painful ending.
"You probably don't feel that way anymore. This is the gap of destiny, Jin Runcandel."
Phaelito turned his head and looked far to the left for a moment. Dante was unconscious in a forest far away, having been blown off by the third Heavenly Destroyer's shock.
"Your friend seems to be running out of strength. And you don't have much left."

Phaelito sent his sword energy towards the forest where Dante had fallen. Jin didn't have the strength to block it. The sword energy, like a typhoon, whipped the entire forest and disappeared into a dot.
"Dante... even Hedo and Gyeongdo won't die with just that."
"Think as you please. But contrary to your words, you have a pretty pleasing face. I can feel your sadness, you know they're dead."

In fact, after the sword energy passed, Dante's faint energy that was felt disappeared. All the divine people hiding in the forest also lost their lives. Jin could feel all of that as if it happened right in front of his eyes.
Unbeknownst to Jin himself, he was shedding tears.

"There's one thing I still don't understand about you. Why are you so sad? I understand about Dante Hairan and the fragments of the old order, but the other humans I killed today weren't that precious to you. You've been shuddering at their deaths since earlier."
"I have a responsibility."

"Responsibility? Ah, I heard that answer earlier, that there's no reason for insects unrelated to the battle of the powerful to be sacrificed. But that's not enough. There must be some other reason for you."
Phaelito was seeing through him accurately.
The heavy emotion that tormented Jin was the guilt of being a 'Returnee'.
"So tell the truth now. Then today, I won't kill any more powerless insects."
